summary.summary: Strongly bullish open expected on convergence of three major catalysts: (1) US-China tariff reductions go into effect TODAY Nov 10 — fentanyl IEEPA tariff drops from 20% to 10%, Section 301 exclusions extended, China suspends all retaliatory ag tariffs; (2) Government shutdown (43 days, longest in history) ending this week with House vote Nov 12 — removes macro uncertainty overhang and restores economic data flow; (3) Q3 earnings season wrapping with 80%+ beat rate and 26% YoY earnings growth in tech/AI. Friday Nov 7 saw S&P 500 fall 1.1% to 6720 as AI infrastructure names pulled back, creating a dip-buy setup into Monday's tariff catalyst.
summary.keyTheme: US-China tariff reduction effective date + government shutdown resolution = dual risk-on catalysts on a Monday following a 1.1% selloff Friday

scenarios.trade: NVDA pulled back 9% from its Oct 29 ATH of $207 to close at $188.15 on Nov 7. The Nov 10 tariff effective date provides a concrete sentiment catalyst — even though Blackwell restrictions remain, the broader trade normalization signals less confrontational US-China relations and reduces tail risk for semiconductor exporters. The stock is the market's AI bellwether and will lead any risk-on rally. AI capex cycle is intact with $200B+ in annual Big Tech spending commitments. The 1.1% S&P selloff Friday creates a gap-fill opportunity. Entry at $192 (gap-up buy) with target at $200 round number.

scenarios.implication: Meta reportedly exploring non-NVDA AI chips. Blackwell export restrictions remain in place. Continued momentum selling from Oct highs could resume after any bounce. If broader market doesn't hold gains, NVDA reverts to $185 support. Earnings next week could disappoint.

scenarios.trade: This is the highest risk-reward setup of the week. Cisco at $71 is near its November low, creating a low-risk entry for a known earnings beat 2 days later. The $1.3B AI order book validates Cisco's pivot to AI networking infrastructure. Guidance for Q2 ($15-15.2B vs $14.6B est) is substantially above consensus. The trade deal also supports global enterprise networking demand. Entry at $71.50 Monday with hold through Wednesday earnings. ACTUAL: Nov 10 opened $71.39, closed $71.07 (flat day) — clean entry at low. Nov 12 close: $73.96 (+4.1% from Nov 10).

scenarios.implication: Market-wide selloff could overwhelm individual earnings beats. Enterprise spending may slow from shutdown aftereffects. If AI order flow is one-time rather than recurring, the 7% move fades. Two-day holding period adds overnight risk.

scenarios.trade: BABA is the largest and most liquid Chinese ADR, making it the primary vehicle for institutional flows on US-China trade normalization. The tariff effective date creates a concrete sentiment catalyst beyond the deal announcement (which came Nov 1). Earnings this week provide a second catalyst. However, ACTUAL data shows Nov 10 was relatively flat (open $167.62, close $165.89, -0.27%), suggesting the trade deal was substantially priced in from the Oct 27 rally when markets hit record highs on deal hopes. This makes the trade lower conviction for a pure day trade — better as a multi-day hold into earnings.

scenarios.implication: Pentagon watchlist concerns surface Nov 14 causing 3.8% drop to $153.80. Profit-taking after 80% YTD run. Political risk remains elevated for Chinese ADRs under Trump administration. Tariff reductions are temporary and could be reversed. Deal was priced in — actual Nov 10 data confirms minimal reaction.

scenarios.trade: Tyson reports before market open with the largest earnings surprise of the week by percentage (37% beat). The simultaneous China agricultural tariff suspension creates a rare double catalyst for a consumer staples name. At $52.68 close, the stock had been range-bound and a blowout quarter breaks it out of the $51-53 range. ACTUAL: opened at $55.40 (5.2% gap-up) confirming the earnings catalyst, but faded to close at $53.90 (+2.31%). Strategy: buy the gap-up and take profit quickly before the fade. Alternatively, wait for mid-morning pullback and buy the $54 dip for a target of $55.50.

scenarios.implication: Revenue miss ($13.9B vs $14B) overshadows EPS beat. Sell-the-news reaction — actual data confirms gap-up then fade. Soybean/ag trade already priced in per muted futures reaction. Food sector stocks rarely sustain gap-up moves.

scenarios.trade: Apple is the single most exposed mega-cap to US-China tariffs due to its Chinese manufacturing footprint. The stock previously rallied 24% on the initial trade deal announcement. However, ACTUAL Nov 10 data shows open at $269.80 and close at $268.47 (-0.48%), indicating the tariff catalyst was fully priced in from the late-October rally. This makes Apple a LOWER conviction day trade — the R:R doesn't justify the position for a single-day hold. Better as a swing trade through late November where it reaches $278+ by month-end.

scenarios.implication: Already rallied 24% on initial deal announcement — upside exhausted near-term. Actual Nov 10 data shows slight decline. Tariff relief is temporary (through Nov 2026) and could be reversed. Valuation stretched at $4T+ market cap. iPhone 17 cycle uncertainty.

watchlist.reason: China soybean commitment supports long-term farm equipment demand. But actual Nov 10 gapped DOWN (open $464 vs prior close $475), closing at $468. Not participating in risk-on. Farmers remain cautious on capex. Avoid for day trade.

watchlist.reason: OpenAI multiyear custom chip deal is bullish. AI infrastructure beneficiary. No specific Nov 10 catalyst but strong sector positioning. Watch for pullback entry.

watchlist.reason: AI cloud infrastructure demand booming, 110% revenue growth, but unprofitable and volatile post-IPO. Better as earnings event trade later this week rather than day trade.

watchlist.reason: Record fiscal year, AI semiconductor equipment demand. Reports later in November. China revenue declining but still substantial at 25% of Q4. Watch for pre-earnings setup.

avoidList.reason: AVOID LONG — reports earnings Nov 13 and stock drops 7-8% on parks/linear TV weakness, revenue miss of $22.5B vs expectations. Streaming was the bright spot (Disney+ +3.8M subs, streaming OI +39%) but insufficient to offset overall disappointment. Do NOT hold into earnings.
